about: The shared commands of the application. A shared command does nothing by itself: a plugin handles it with an entry of contributes.handlers and registers the handler under the id of the command. Run over a target, a command with one matching handler runs it, and a command with several offers the matching handlers as its items. `arguments` are declared once, as a manifest command declares them; the palette asks for them and the core checks them for every handler. tools/commands.mjs writes the Go and TypeScript lists from this file. `appCommands` are the commands of the application that take arguments, declared the same way; an argument of the type `enum` lists its allowed values in `options`, as a setting of a manifest does. The entry of a slot that passes values to an `app:` command is checked against them and against the `arguments` of the shared command of that id, and an `app:` command with neither takes none.
